newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul tightens reserve rules for commercial banks.
newsitem.headline: Seoul tightens reserve rules for commercial banks.

text.p: South Korea's Office of Bank Supervision said on Friday it would raise the minimum ratio of evaluated losses from share holding that commercial banks have to account for in their income statements.
For the first half of this year, commercial banks will be required to account for at least 40 percent of evaluated losses, up from 30 percent at the end of 1996, the office said.
The ratio would be raised by 15 percentage points every six months, reaching 100 percent at the end of June 1999, it said.
In the past, the office had set the minimum ratio ahead of the end of every half-year, it said.
